idea: Little science wonder – WIND (SUNNY PARK, Ava in OUTDOOR pink overalls): a gust of wind makes Baby Ava's colorful toy pinwheel (red, yellow, blue, green) spin round and round beside her face ('Whoosh! Wow! My pinwheel spins!'); the wind stops and the pinwheel stops ('Oh no! It stopped! No more wind!'); she makes her own wind and blows on it – copy-me 'Blow, blow, blow! Round and round! Blow with me!'; orange and yellow autumn leaves swirl around her ('Whoosh, whoosh! The leaves dance too!'); she asks the viewer 'What makes them move? Hmm?' (2 s humming pause) – 'The wind! The wind! Whoosh, whoosh!'; lesson 'I can't see the wind, but I see it move!'; copy-me 'Wave your arms like the wind! Yay!'. Loop: the hook framing again with the pinwheel spinning, 'Bye bye, wind! Bye bye, friends!'.
title: Whoosh! My Pinwheel Spins! 🌬️ What Is Wind? Science for Toddlers with Baby Ava | Crayon Babies
description:
Whoosh! A gust of wind makes Baby Ava's pinwheel spin round and round in Sunny Park – then the wind stops! 🌬️ So Ava blows, blow, blow, blow, and makes her very own wind. Can you guess what makes the leaves dance?

🎬 What happens in this video:
🌬️ Whoosh! The wind spins Ava's red, yellow, blue and green pinwheel
😮 Oh no! The wind stopped – and so did the pinwheel
💨 Blow, blow, blow! Blow with Ava and make it spin again
🍂 The leaves dance in the wind – "What makes them move? Hmm?"
👋 Wave your arms like the wind – then bye bye, wind!

📚 Kids learn: wind is moving air – we can't see it, but we can see it move things • wind • blow • spin • round and round • leaves

🎶 Voices only: children singing, humming and clapping with a soft hand drum – no other musical instruments.

A fun little science song for toddlers and preschoolers about the wind: blow on a pinwheel, watch the leaves dance, answer the question and wave your arms like the wind with Baby Ava.
